w10_T4_002282: On Saturday morning Ike set up his fruit stall with 5 boxes of oranges, 109 oranges in each box. Jay's stall across the aisle had 9 times as many oranges as Ike's, so Jay had by far the bigger display. Jay's stall is 4 metres long. In the afternoon Jay sold 4849 oranges to a juice company. In the evening he gave 51 oranges to the market cleaners. How many oranges did Jay have left?
w10_T4_002284: Kit's front flower bed has 135 tulips, 27 daffodils, and 66 crocuses. She has 3 beds altogether, and the other beds are planted exactly the same way, which took her a dozen weekends. For the spring fair she cut 621 flowers from the beds, and after that 71 new flowers opened. How many flowers are in Kit's beds now?
w10_T4_002286: Lea had 152 dollars and spent 144 dollars on a winter coat. She then received 32 dollars for tutoring and 35 dollars from her grandmother. Her brother Max has 5 times as much money as Lea has now, so Max is much better off than Lea. How many dollars does Max have?
w10_T4_002289: In the morning 4 lorries arrived at the building site, each carrying 8 pallets with 196 bricks on every pallet, and the bricklayers used 4896 bricks before lunch. The site is 15 kilometres from the brickworks. In the afternoon a labourer found 37 bricks in an old skip and added them to the stock, and 21 bricks were broken by a forklift. In the evening the foreman sold every brick left in the stock to a neighbouring site at 6 cents a brick. How many cents did the foreman receive?
w10_T4_002294: In the morning Nat had 119 flyers for the school play and handed out 48 of them at the bus stop. The print shop then gave her 2 times as many flyers as she had left, replacing her stack with the larger one. In the afternoon she handed out 73 flyers at the shopping centre. In the evening her friend gave her 74 flyers that had been left over from another stack. How many flyers does Nat have now?
w10_T4_002296: Ola's team started the board game with 126 points and lost 113 points on a disastrous turn. In the bonus round every point they still had became worth 8 points. A penalty then cost them 89 points. The game lasted 40 minutes. In the final round every point they held became worth 9 points, and a dozen cheering supporters watched them collect a 71-point prize on the last square. How many points did Ola's team finish with?
w10_T4_002297: In the morning Pam checked the bus fare for her new route: 44 cents for the first zone plus 39 cents for the second zone. Because she travels there and back, her daily fare is 2 times the single fare. In the afternoon she found that a family pass halves the daily fare, and she bought one. She travels on 5 days each week. In the evening she loaded a week's fares onto her card, which charges a 19-cent loading fee. Pam counts in cents rather than dollars, remembering that one hundred cents make a dollar. How many cents did the weekly loading cost her?
w10_T4_002299: A pump at the reservoir moves 181 litres of water every minute, and 4 identical pumps run side by side. The pumps run for 5 minutes in each cycle, and there are 8 cycles a day. All of the day's water is shared equally among the 4 farms that draw from the reservoir, and Quinn's farm is one of them; her daily share is more water than Rae's well can provide for Rae's farm. The water board records amounts in litres rather than millilitres, since one thousand millilitres make a litre. How many litres does Quinn's farm receive each day?
w10_T4_002307: In the morning Sol counted the trees in his orchard: 3 rows with 73 trees in each, plus 3 trees by the barn and 80 young trees in the new field. That is more trees than his neighbour Tom has in his whole orchard. In the afternoon Sol reckoned that every tree would fill 4 crates and that each crate holds 5 kilograms of fruit. In the evening, after the harvest came in exactly as he expected, he sold 1427 kilograms to a cider maker. How many kilograms of fruit does Sol have left?
w10_T4_002309: In the morning at Tara's stall, each customer paid 137 cents for a bag of nuts plus a 4-cent bag charge, and 8 customers bought a bag. In the afternoon one customer paid 69 cents for a cup of tea and another paid 70 cents for a pastry. Tara's takings were exactly the same on each of the 3 days of the fair. In the evening of the last day she paid 2962 cents for her pitch. Tara keeps her takings in cents rather than dollars, remembering that one hundred cents make a dollar. How many cents does Tara have left from the fair?
w10_T4_002310: In the morning the recycling centre received 9 crates of glass bottles with 216 bottles in each crate. The delivery lorry is 10 years old. In the afternoon a volunteer brought in 3 bottles from her car and a cafe dropped off 47 more. In the evening the centre paid out the deposit of 8 cents on every bottle it had received that day. How many cents did the centre pay out?
w10_T4_002314: Una had 167 dollars in her savings account and withdrew 117 dollars to pay for a course. Her employer's savings scheme then made her balance 4 times what it was. She deposited 69 dollars from selling old books and paid a 2-dollar bank fee. She then split her balance equally among 3 new accounts, one for each of her goals, and the travel account received its share. How many dollars are in Una's travel account?
w10_T4_002315: In the morning Vera filled 9 trays with 156 seedlings each in her first greenhouse, then added 76 seedlings from a spare tray and 14 seedlings that had sprouted in pots. In the afternoon she confirmed that all 4 of her greenhouses were stocked exactly like the first, and she planted 75 more seedlings by the door. In the evening Vera visited Wil's nursery, which has 3 times as many seedlings as Vera has in total, so Wil's nursery is much bigger than hers. How many seedlings does Wil's nursery have?
w10_T4_002328: Xu's phone plan gave him 186 minutes of calls this month, though he thinks a dozen minutes would be enough for most people. He used 59 minutes calling his parents, 39 minutes on a work call, and 35 minutes on a call to the bank. He then bought a 14-minute top-up and later a 27-minute top-up. The plan shows the balance in minutes rather than hours, and sixty minutes make one hour. How many minutes does Xu have left?
w10_T4_002329: Yara brought 188 handmade mugs to the craft fair and sold 106 of them in the first hour. Her partner then delivered 70 more mugs, and she sold 146 mugs in the afternoon. The stall rent was 30 dollars. At closing time she sold every remaining mug to a cafe owner for 4 dollars each. How many dollars did the cafe owner pay?
w10_T4_002331: Zoe puts 230 cents into her holiday jar every day, but she takes 100 cents back out each day for her bus fare. She kept this up for 9 days. She then took 298 cents from the jar for a birthday present and 168 cents for a cinema ticket. Zoe counts her jar in cents rather than dollars, since one hundred cents make a dollar. How many cents are in the jar now?
w10_T4_002332: Abe's bakery bakes 162 buns on each tray, 4 trays in each oven, and it has 2 ovens, so one batch fills both ovens. On top of each batch the bakers shape 70 buns by hand. The bakery makes 6 batches a day plus 23 sample buns for the counter. It bakes 7 days a week, which is more buns than Bea's bakery down the road manages in a month. How many buns does Abe's bakery make in a week?
w10_T4_002344: Cy's lorry carries 229 boxes on each of its 8 shelves, and Cy runs 2 lorries loaded exactly the same way. The boxes from both lorries are shared equally among 4 depots. Each box holds 6 jars of jam. Dee's warehouse holds 2 times as many jars of jam as one of those depots receives, so Dee's warehouse is the bigger stock. How many jars of jam does Dee's warehouse hold?
w10_T4_002345: In the morning Ed's stall had 91 pies on the counter, but 6 pies were dropped and 68 pies were sold. In the afternoon Ed baked until he had 6 times as many pies as were left, and his mother brought 23 more pies from home. In the evening his brother matched the stock exactly, so Ed had 2 times as many pies as before. How many pies does Ed have now?
w10_T4_002348: In the morning Fay timed her walk to school: 34 minutes to the bridge and 7 minutes from the bridge to the gate. Since she walks there and back, her daily walking is 2 times that. In the afternoon her friend Gus worked out that he walks 2 times as far as Fay does in a day, so Gus does more walking than Fay. Gus walks that daily amount on all 7 days of the week. In the evening Gus also walked 35 minutes to a friend's house. Gus records his walking in minutes rather than hours, since sixty minutes make one hour. How many minutes did Gus walk this week?
w10_T4_002350: In the morning Hal's grandmother shared 35 dollars equally among her 5 grandchildren, and Hal got his share. Hal spent 1 dollar on sweets and then split what he had left equally among his 6 savings envelopes, one for each goal. In the afternoon his father put 77 dollars into Hal's holiday envelope. In the evening his aunt added 49 dollars to the same envelope. How many dollars are in Hal's holiday envelope now?
w10_T4_002352: In the morning Ivy's gift shop had 238 candles on its shelves, which was more than Jo's shop next door had in stock. Ivy sold 108 candles before lunch, and 10 candles were broken by a customer. In the afternoon a delivery of 54 candles arrived. In the evening Ivy unpacked 33 candles from the storeroom onto the shelves. How many candles are on Ivy's shelves now?
w10_T4_002353: A gardener sowed 159 pea seeds, sharing them equally among 3 beds, and every seed in the first bed grew into a plant. Each plant produced 5 pods, and each pod held 9 peas. The gardener also picked 57 peas from a stray plant by the fence. She has 5 gardens that each produced exactly the same as this one, after a dozen years of careful work. How many peas did she pick from all 5 gardens?
w10_T4_002354: Kai's training lap is 85 metres long, and he runs 6 laps every session. He trains on 7 days a week and kept that up for twice as long as he first planned, 2 weeks in all. His running shoes cost 90 dollars. On the last day he also ran 6 extra metres to the finish line. How many metres did Kai run in total?
w10_T4_002359: Lin's delivery van covers 187 kilometres on its regular weekly route, plus 18 kilometres to the depot and 62 kilometres to the coast each week. She drove that same weekly distance for 8 weeks, which is more than Mia's van covered in the same time. In the last week she also drove 41 kilometres to a special delivery. How many kilometres did Lin's van cover over those 8 weeks?
